items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?
items.label: Ponderosa Music
items._cn_summary: Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino成立五十周年的纪念专辑，由第二代核心人物小提琴兼手鼓演奏家Mauro Durante主导，重新编排乐队过去数十年间的经典曲目。父亲Daniele和母亲Rina创作的标题曲由父子两代音乐人共同演绎，早期歌手Rossella Pinto回归演唱《Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare》。专辑保留了pizzica音乐干燥而富有包围感的原声底色，编曲中加入了合成贝斯等电声元素，并重新混音了2014年与钢琴家Ludovico Einaudi合作的Taranta项目曲目。整体制作横跨传统与当下，既向乐队历史致敬，也展示了新一代乐手对声音色彩和编排逻辑的拓展。这张作品属于南意大利区域性传统的世界音乐范畴，在保持原声核心的同时逐步走向全球化舞台。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku暌违多年推出的第四张专辑，融合北欧民谣与巴尔干音乐传统。专辑标题意为介于瞬间与一段时间之间的模糊时段。她原创的《Finsko Dajchovo》借鉴保加利亚民间舞蹈节奏，轻快灵动；《Seitsemän》取材自马其顿情歌，充满春日般的希望。Niku展现出敏锐的旋律感，《Elokuu》以挽歌式笔触描绘八月夏末光线，暗示冬日将至的忧郁。多首波尔卡舞曲与开篇阴郁短曲《Ohto》形成对照。专辑核心是终曲《Poloneesi äidille》，Niku在母亲七十岁生日前三年为其创作，母亲去世后此曲成为安魂之作，当她开始演唱时，音乐升华为超越性的情感表达。独立厂牌发行，整体呈现跨界民族音乐融合的个人化探索。

items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

items._cn_summary: 克里特里拉琴演奏家Stelios Petrakis的器乐专辑，标题《Lyric》点明其抒情核心。他不仅是顶尖的里拉琴与鲁特琴演奏家，也是知名乐器制作师，与Ross Daly合作开发了带共鸣弦的改良里拉琴。专辑以传统克里特旋律为根基，邀请来自不同时空的杰出音乐人共同演绎——包括伊朗zarb鼓手Bijan Chemirani、布列塔尼管乐演奏家Sylvain Barou、瓦伦西亚曼陀林手Efrén López及亚美尼亚、希腊等地乐手，融合竖琴、低音提琴、手风琴等多种乐器。开篇曲《Astro Sti Gaza》由其兄弟Yannis填词，呼唤和平。专辑在保持传统旋律骨架的同时，通过跨文化的器乐编配拓展了克里特音乐的织体与情绪层次，既有行军般的史诗段落，也有塔兰泰拉式的即兴炫技，展现出地中海东部岛屿音乐与世界对话的可能性。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Formed in 2007 and hailing from the post-hardcore scene, the Spanish band Toundra emerged as a breakout act in Spain's underground scene and performed at the 2010 Primavera Sound festival in Barcelona. The proposed sonic experience begins with "Bajamar," alternating between staggered bursts of distorted guitars and harmonic passages, with the drums providing effective accompaniment in both sections. You can feel the psychedelia; you can sense the raw, rocky texture. While the band cites Pelican, another act in the genre, as an influence, I also detect elements of Mogwai."Pleamar" unfolds in a calm, pleasant manner, albeit in black and white, and the guitar work reminded me of Mike McCready from Pearl Jam. It is on "Medusa" that the quartet truly comes together as a unit, fully utilizing the dual-guitar lineup; one can discern the two distinct paths being traced, sometimes intersecting, other times running parallel. At times, Esteban Jim�nez's guitar stands out, almost seeming to speak or gasp for breath. I also detect influences from the Badmotorfinger era of Soundgarden."�rbita" bridges psychedelia and post-rock like a desert storm, full of lightning and thunder but devoid of rain, a dry storm, where Alberto Tocados's bass plays a pivotal role, providing the counterpoints of tension and calm that link the tempestuous passages together."Jaur�a" is the closest thing to a dramatic climax on the album, a moment of heightened tension where the guitars converge to tell a sometimes somber story, a tale without words or time that, while seeming as though it had always existed, reveals itself as new with every listen.
items._cn_summary: 这张2008年的西班牙乐队Toundra首张专辑以纯器乐形式展开，融合了后金属的失真吉他音墙与迷幻、后摇的空间感。《Bajamar》在粗暴的riff段落与和声化旋律之间交替，制造出粗粝与迷幻交织的质感；《Medusa》充分发挥双吉他的对位能力，两条旋律线时而交汇时而平行；贝斯手在《Órbita》中承担了张力与平静之间的桥梁角色；终曲《Jauría》将情绪推向戏剧性高点。整体制作注重器乐之间的互动与情绪铺陈，不依赖人声叙事，乐评将之与Pelican、Mogwai、Soundgarden等后金属及另类摇滚乐队相提并论。

items.body: Review by Progfan97402 — I was wondering if this would ever be accepted into Prog Archives, there's no doubt the music was worthy of inclusion and I'm glad it's now in the database. It's hard for me to think of another prog rock album that is more obscure than this. Apparently, the album did get manufactured by EMI/Electrola (but it had a generic blue label to look more like a private press) so it likely made it into standard record stores in West Germany at the time. The cover to Pacific Prison screams American private press prog album, except this isn't American at all. This does not have that professional polish, so if that's what you're wanting you won't find it here. The vocals definitely do not have that polish, either. What you get is symphonic prog with space rock overtones. Lots of Hammond organ, Elka Rhapsody, and the ARP 2600 synthesizer. It sounds like what would happen if you cross Eloy with Pulsar, and perhaps a bit of Novalis but without the polished production and a more underground feel, this is what you get. There is also some flute as well (more like Pulsar than Jethro Tull). If there is a concept behind this album it's hard telling, but all the songs segue together for one continuous listen, aside from switching from side one to side two if you own the LP. While the the shortcomings are a bit obvious, it doesn't have a great production and it definitely a bit rough around the edges, it's still a nice album worth hearing especially if you don't mind a more underground take on the German symphonic prog/space rock sound.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1978年德国地下发行的交响前卫摇滚专辑，由EMI/Electrola代工压制但刻意采用私人出版外观。乐评描述其音乐以Hammond风琴、Elka Rhapsody和ARP 2600合成器为核心音色，呈现出Eloy与Pulsar混合的气质，带有更粗糙的地下感。专辑中也有长笛演奏，整体定位为带太空摇滚色彩的德式交响前卫。歌曲之间以无缝衔接方式串联成连贯聆听体验，但制作水准有限、人声缺乏润饰，瑕疵明显。乐评认为尽管制作粗糙、概念模糊，对于不介意地下质感、偏好德式交响前卫与太空摇滚融合的听众来说，仍是值得一听的作品。整体属于小众类型档案记录性质的音乐文献。

items.body: Dead Voices on Air, the project of Mark Spybey, will release a new album, “Mothcomma”, worldwide through Re:Mission Entertainment on 17 July 2026. The 12-track album comes out on CD and in digital form, with pre-orders open at Bandcamp and the project’s Big Cartel store. Dead Voices on Air recorded “Mothcomma” in the aftermath of the project’s 2025 US tour, with sessions split between the Tees Valley in North East England and Lafayette, Colorado. The album was made on both sides of the Atlantic, and mixes the project’s experimental, industrial and dark ambient elements, moving between song structures, ambient passages, hand-built rhythms and treated vocals. Named tracks include “Pas de Chasse”, the title track “Mothcomma” and “For the Rush of Black Tar”. Mothcomma by Dead Voices on Air Recording and credits behind Dead Voices on Air ‘Mothcomma’ The album credits Nathan Jamiel, Mark Spybey and Stephen Weatherall, with additional contributions from Robert Galbraith and Elizabeth Virosa of Snowbeasts and from Lori Cole. Robert Galbraith mastered the record. Nathan Jamiel, of the Denver band The Drood, and Stephen Weatherall have contributed to the project’s last two albums and played Spybey’s autumn 2025 US concerts. Pre-orders run through Bandcamp and the Big Cartel store, where the “Mothcomma” CD is listed alongside a new run of t-shirts. Stock is limited: some items ship from the United States and others directly from Spybey in the UK, and the first 40 orders include a Dead Voices on Air logo sticker. About Dead Voices on Air Dead Voices on Air formed in Vancouver in 1992, when Mark Spybey, who had played in Newcastle’s Zoviet France in the late 1980s, began the project with Scott Harker and Clancy Dennehey. It became the ongoing vehicle for Spybey’s experimental, industrial and dark ambient work. Spybey was also an original member of Download, the offshoot featuring Skinny Puppy’s cEvin Key, and recorded under the name Propeller. Across more than three decades, Spybey has collaborated widely, working with Graham Lewis of Wire, Faust, Michael Rother of Neu!, Dieter Moebius of Cluster, Jarboe of Swans, Jochen Arbeit of Einstürzende Neubauten, Lee Scratch Perry, Pigface and Snowbeasts. He has released through labels including Cold Spring, Soleilmoon, Kranky, Nettwerk, Emergency Hearts and Re:Mission Entertainment, and works with Zoviet France co-founder Robin Storey as Reformed Faction. In 2022 Emergency Hearts published Spybey’s musical memoir “Explicit in Purpose”. Side-Line has followed the project in recent years, from the 2022 re-release of its debut as “Abrader Redux” to the 2023 collaborative album “Pennine” with Xqui, and spoke with Spybey for a 2021 ‘Click Interview’. In spring 2023 Spybey formed DADU with friends from his home town; Nathan Jamiel and Stephen Weatherall, who feature on “Mothcomma”, came out of that circle and toured the US with him in 2025. “Mothcomma” is the project’s newest release for Re:Mission Entertainment.
items._cn_summary: 这是Dead Voices on Air新专辑《Mothcomma》的新闻发布稿，由Mark Spybey主导。专辑于英美两地录音，融合了实验、工业与暗氛围元素，在歌曲结构、环境段落、手工节奏与处理过的人声之间自由切换。十二首曲目通过小厂牌Re:Mission Entertainment以CD和数字形式发行，预购附带限量贴纸。参与录制的有长期合作者及Snowbeasts成员。本文为新专辑预告性质的信息公告，并非深度评论，涉及内容偏向发行信息与合作者背景介绍，未对专辑声音设计或音乐性进行实质分析。

items.body: British electro-industrial group Portion Control have released “Tex-Mex (Live at Dolce Vita, Lausanne 6/12/85)“, the second single from their archival box set “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…“, out 14 August 2026 on Artoffact Records. The set collects the London group’s mid-1980s work across a 4xCD box, a digital edition and a limited red vinyl LP. You can stream and pre-order the box set through the Bandcamp player below. 1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge… by Portion Control Portion Control detail ‘Tex-Mex’ and the box set “Tex-Mex” was recorded in December 1985 at the Dolce Vita in Lausanne, a Swiss venue that had opened earlier that year, and the performance was filmed. The band trace the track back to their studio sessions of the period rather than the stage. “‘Tex-Mex’ was recorded as part of the ‘..Step Forward’ recording sessions at Guerilla Studios in Little Venice, London,” the band recall. “It was where William Orbit had his recording base at the time and we utilised a lot of the equipment he had set up there for his own early electronic work.” A video for the single accompanies the release. The box set, “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, gathers 77 tracks. It brings together the 1983 mini-LP “Hit The Pulse”, the albums “..Step Forward” (1984) and “Psycho Bod Saves The World” (1986), the 12-inch singles “The Great Divide”, “Go-Talk” and “Raise The Pulse”, and the “Purge” EP (1986), alongside B-sides, compilation tracks, rarities, remixes, demos and two live recordings, from Amsterdam in 1984 and Lausanne in 1985. Paul Lavigne remastered all 77 tracks at Kontrast Mastering; 16 are previously unreleased and a further 12 appear on CD and digital for the first time. The 4xCD edition comes in a five-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet designed by Stefan Alt of Ant-Zen, and the red vinyl LP carries ten key tracks. “Tex-Mex” follows “Refugee”, a version reworked by Rhys Fulber of Front Line Assembly that Portion Control issued as the first single in June 2026. The reissue campaign continues the group’s move to Artoffact, which began when Portion Control joined Artoffact Records and released the “SEED EP3.1” EP in December 2025. About Portion Control Portion Control formed in London in 1979 and built a raw, minimal sound around sequenced synthesisers, samplers and strident vocals. Their early records – the 1982 debut album “I Staggered Mentally”, the “Hit The Pulse” mini-LP (1983) and the second album “..Step Forward” (1984) – placed them among the pioneers of hard-edged electronic dance music, and the group supported Depeche Mode on tour in 1984. Their use of early sampling and drum-machine technology fed into the work of later acts including Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails and Orbital. After a hiatus that began in the late 1980s, Portion Control returned in 2004 with “Wellcome”, followed by “Filthy White Guy” (2006), “Pure Form” (2012) and the run of “SEED” EPs between 2020 and 2025. The group signed to Artoffact Records in late 2025, and the label is now reissuing their catalogue as a series of box sets. “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” is the first of those sets, and “Tex-Mex” is the second single drawn from it.

items.body: On the Pull Up Riddim EP, Italian production duo Mellow Mood, made up of twins Jacopo and Lorenzo Garzia, revive the traditional Jamaican compilation format by running five different vocalists over the exact same instrumental groove. German-Peruvian singer INTI Ayvar Waltz takes the final slot with “My Opinion”, using his three and a half minutes over the shared beat to deliver a blunt message about global conflict and a call for cohexistance. Waltz speaks directly to the entire global population, contrasting a child’s right to play with the reality of warfare and rejecting religion as a justification for violence. The hook, “You don’t have to share my opinion”, makes room for disagreement, and the song settles on the fact that people can coexist and judge each other. Waltz sings from Cologne, bringing the clear vocal style that led reggae veteran Luciano to call him “the Golden Voice” onstage last year. The Garzia twins originally built this underlying loop from “Pull Up“, their Romain Virgo collaboration from the 2025 album 7. Recorded and mixed by Paolo Baldini DubFiles at Alambic Conspiracy Studio in Pordenone, the track lands alongside Mellow Mood’s summer live schedule, including upcoming stops in Italy in Genoa, Naples, Rome, and at the Marquês de Pombal Palace in Oeiras, Portugal. Stream “My Opinion” HERE and get the Pull Up Riddim EP following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: INTI Ayvar Waltz x MELLOW MOOD – My Opinion (Pull Up Riddim) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Review by kev rowland — I wrote to Llyn Y Morynion after I reviewed the brilliant debut album in the last issue, so imagine my delight when I received in the post this their new CD. If anything, this is better than the debut! Llyn mix so many different styles and mould them into something that is old, yet at the same time is refreshingly new. English folk seems to be taking a larger part this time, and there is even more use of acoustic guitar, but this provides the light to what can be heavy darkness. It is the darkness that seems to be most rooted in 1972, taking all the best bits of the prog, rock, folk boom of the late Sixties and coming up with a real gem. Matthias Jungkunz has a wonderfully clear voice, and this shows on "Grows An Oak", where it is the vocals that carry the song. Delicate use of a flute helps to build a classic ambience of almost Horslips proportions. I cannot stress too highly just what a wonderful band this is.Originally appeared in Feedback #39, January 1997

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是威尔士乐队Llyn Y Morynion的第二张作品，将英式民谣元素与七十年代前卫摇滚的厚重质感相融合。原声吉他的运用为整体增添了一层轻盈的质地，与乐队偏好的黑暗、厚重段落形成对比。主唱Matthias Jungkunz的嗓音清澈透明，在曲目中承担了主要的叙事和情感传递功能。专辑中也融入了长笛乐器，营造出与爱尔兰民谣摇滚乐队Horslips相近的古典氛围。整体风格根植于六十年代末至七十年代初的前卫、民谣、摇滚融合浪潮，试图在复古根基上寻找新鲜感。从制作角度看，这是一张风格杂糅的跨界前卫作品，将民谣旋律引入前卫摇滚框架中进行实验。

items.body: Review by Deadwing — It's probably one of my favourite albums from them, which is a big surprise, especially after two very very weak releases which killed any expectations from them.The Wow! Signal brings the band back to composing songs with more coherent arrangements. It's a much better paced album where songs transitions well between each other and have properly build-up. It's still very eclectic and it definitely doesn't sounds like any of their "classic" albums, though! The closest to the "classic" formula is probably songs like Cryogen and the final track, Space Debris.From the epic orchestral intro of The Dark Forest, the bombastic bass of Nightshift Superstar, the over-the-top 80's Hexagons, which leads to 2 very heavy tracks The Sickness in you & I and Unraveling (the best 3 track sequence from the album) to the introspective Space Debris, it's a fresh pot of ideas and great instrumentation.It might not be "progressive" enough for some, but there's a lot to appreciate regarding genre blending, interesting textures, competent instrumentation and a well structured album composition.9/10 to me.
items._cn_summary: MUSE 乐队在经历两张口碑不佳的作品后，以《The Wow! Signal》回归较为成熟的创作路径。整张专辑在编曲上强调歌曲结构的连贯性，乐曲之间的过渡自然，起承转合安排得当。乐评人指出，虽然作品仍保持乐队一贯的折衷主义风格，但与早期经典作品的关联较为疏远，只有《Cryogen》和结尾曲《Space Debris》较接近以往的路数。专辑编排呈现段落化推进的特征：从管弦乐式史诗开场，到放克贝斯主导的曲目，再到过载的80年代合成器段落，进而转入两首重型作品，形成专辑中最突出的三曲连续序列，最终收束于内省气质的长篇作品。在器乐配置上展现了扎实的演奏功底与多类型融合的企图，但对偏好极端实验、前卫即兴或电子前沿制作的听众而言，其'前卫'含量有限。

items.body: Review by tszirmay — Many prog musicians have had day jobs as well as careers, and some are still toiling whilst including their musical talents as a passionate hobby or a side project. Doctor Greenwood still practices as a burn surgeon at the Royal Adelaide Hospital in Australia, as well as getting to record with Unitopia, arguably Down-Under's 'eminence grise' (French for grey matter) when it comes to contemporary prog. On the recently released and promptly reviewed 'Seven Chambers', Greenwood's fretboard contributions added a massive impulse to the crafty tracks relating to the human heart and its seven ventricles! As befits many solo ventures, historically a personal opportunity to display a wider variety of stylistic variations, Dr. John ("are we in the right place?") offers a palette of differing vignettes, as well as his multi-instrumentalist skills and some heartfelt lyrical content in the form of Dark Blue, which was gracefully adorned with a foreword from some artist called Steve Hackett, none the less. On board guests include Sean Timms on keys, master drummer Craig Blundell as well as locals skin beaters Ben Todd and Mike Giuffreda, bass guitar from Nick Sinclair and gypsy violin from Julian Ferraretto, each on one track. Family members complete the cast, thus giving this album a peculiar homey sheen.Diving straight into the Covid mismanagement 'controversy', Dark Blue kicks off with an elongated 12 minute + treatise on the rather unfit global health industry, a subject matter that surely comes easy for the good doctor. Orchestrated in a typical progressive quarantine, switching between symphonic sweeps and sweet vaudevillian humour, nursing powerful lyrics with hygienic mellotron sheets and infused with a melancholic acoustic guitar recovery, this is quite the anaesthetic! Especially noticeable in the IV fluid outro. Change of pace into a stage production of theatrical operations, a trio of interconnected tracks with a swirling violin first on the intricately woven "Too Late!" with whimsical vocals and intense child-like narration, loaded to the gills with dense atmosphere and mellifluous audacity, sliced open with a honed guitar scalpel. This blends into the orchestral "Too Late! Reprise", a surgical flute adding to the cinematographic score and setting up the colossal epic, 16 minutes of proggy bliss on "the Ocean", led by John's daughter Emma, whose crystalline voice navigates the waves with brave resolve. Gigantic sonic thunderclaps smash into the surging white caps, courageously surviving until a weary piano indicates calmer waters ahead, John handling the microphone with relieved conviction. Interweaving flutes, church bells tolling on the mainland, guiding the ship home in the thick fog, as a delicate acoustic guitar welcomes back the protagonists, voices in tow. The sailor and the siren. The extensive and shimmering electric axe solo soars above the mellotron choirs with heavenly grace and carves a sumptuous melody to expunge over. A poignant vocal finale seals the deal. Things get personal on the next trio of tracks, starting with the solemn "Requiem", a thoughtfully orchestrated lament, a platform for both versions of the fretboard to glide along the synthesized structure with veneration. The guitars are exceptional, to say the very least. On the other side of the scale, the irritated "Heartless" is a harrowing plea for pain caused, ruthlessly hard in both intent, vocal delivery, and instrumental prowess. It's a pungent and urgent track that hits the spot. "Inside" is really a tale of two styles, a section that has a stage production, 'listen to me story' feel, accessible and straightforward, as the focus is on the words, very the Beatles-ish. The instrumental transitions are punchy and intense. "Packing my Suitcase" also has the Beatles-like whimsy (think Bungalow Bill, Rocky Raccoon) and serves to entertain, without too much thought and complexity. The gypsy violin does its duty accordingly. "The Kiss" is an interlude for acoustic guitar and a Nick Magnus orchestration. Very pastoral, very English, very pristine. Then comes the surprise! The Genesis classic "Afterglow" is the proud owner of one of those melodies that cannot simply be corrupted by alternate sounding covers (a bit like Nights in White Satin, Starless, or Whiter Shade of Pale), as there is no room for improvement of any possible kind. As such, it has a tremendously poignant tribute feel to which many other artists have been respectful, and John is no exception. A track that promotes the reverential notion of timeless classic and justice is done. The guitar solo is appropriately grandiose, soothing the soul like the finest panacea. The album should have stopped here, as it's a tough act to follow. Nevertheless, "A Proper Song" puts up quite a courageous fight, a dreamy swirl with sincere lyrics, ("if I want to hear a choir, I'll go to church" LOL), churning organ and a glittering axe solo but its so honestly fun that one cannot quibble. The disc ends with a John Greenwood kiss, dark bluesy lips on the suitcase sticker, going far away, to the Land Down Under. 4.5 Indigo Travels
items._cn_summary: John Greenwood 是澳大利亚皇家阿德莱德医院的烧伤外科医生，业余时间以音乐人身份活动，曾与南澳前卫名团 Unitopia 合作。这张《Dark Blue》以新冠疫情医疗危机为开篇，用十二分钟以上的长篇编曲展开，交响铺陈与杂耍式幽默交替，歌词犀利，配以美乐托琴音垫与忧郁木吉他段落。专辑中段以三首联曲展开戏剧化叙事，吉普赛小提琴与长笛穿梭其中，十六分钟史诗曲目《The Ocean》由其女儿 Emma 担任主唱，以水晶般的人声驾驭海浪般的音墙，最终在钢琴与原声吉他引导下回归平静。整张专辑融合了多种乐器与家庭成员参与制作，带有温馨的手工质感，前卫摇滚骨架内融入古典配器与剧场元素，适合喜欢长篇叙事型前卫作品的听众。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — All-acoustic solo guitar music (except for the two-minute piano piece entitled "Piano Improvisation") performed on Larry's new Ovation guitars--both 6-stringed and 12-stringed. It is an album that Larry was always very proud of--which made me listen to it with serious attention. There is some fine guitar playing here, often performed on multiple tracks (all with his own guitar playing)--some of which has relevance to the Jazz-Rock Fusion world. and much of which is likable (like his albums with Philip Catherine and Joe Beck and John Scofield)--but just not enough inside the scope of J-R F to be recommended as such.Favorite songs: the 12-string strum-backed blues BYRDS tribute, 2. items._cn_summary: 这是一张Larry Coryell的纯原声吉他独奏专辑，演奏使用六弦和十二弦Ovation吉他完成，仅含一段两分钟的钢琴即兴。全专辑由Coryell本人通过多轨录音叠加完成，部分曲目与印度小提琴家Lakshmi Subramanian合作，带有南亚音乐元素，被乐评比作Shakti的风格。曲目多为旋律性较强的器乐作品，包括向The Byrds致敬的布鲁斯风格十二弦曲、炫技性的多重吉他演奏，以及以莫扎特为灵感的十二弦作品。整体制作精良，吉他演奏技巧出色，但在爵士摇滚融合范畴内探索有限，更偏向原声吉他独奏与跨文化合作的小品集，适合Coryell的爱好者收藏，对一般融合乐迷而言并非必听之作。

items.body: Parallel 33 released “Sowe”, a dark post-punk single, on 26 June 2026 through Mania Records. The track runs 2:27 and is available on Spotify and Apple Music. “Sowe” is the sixth single from the project, which started releasing music in 2025. Parallel 33 credit three writers on ‘Sowe’ On “Sowe”, Michael Zamora plays guitar and Limbert Palomino wrote the lyrics and sings, while ALEO produced the track and shares the writing credit. In the release announcement, ALEO describes the single as “a slow, dark, moody post-punk cut about falling in and out of love with the same person year after year”. The announcement lists Joy Division, She Past Away and Molchat Doma as reference points. About Parallel 33 Parallel 33 is a dark post-punk project that releases through Mania Records. The single “Sowe” credits Michael Zamora on guitar, Limbert Palomino on vocals and lyrics, and ALEO as producer. The project describes itself as making “restless tracks for restless nights”. Parallel 33 began issuing singles in 2025, starting with “Vampira” in March 2025, followed by “Fin” in April 2025 and “Come Alive” in August 2025. The project moved to a faster pace in 2026, releasing “The Calling” on 24 April, “Raquel” on 15 May and “Sowe” on 26 June. “Vampira” remains its most-streamed track on Spotify. With “Sowe”, Parallel 33 extends a run of dark post-punk singles into the second half of 2026.
items._cn_summary: Parallel 33 通过 Mania Records 厂牌发行单曲《Sowe》，定位为暗黑后朋克风格，时长仅两分半，结构紧凑。该作由 Michael Zamora 担任吉他、Limbert Palomino 负责人声与歌词、ALEO 制作并参与创作。制作人将曲目描述为缓慢、阴暗、情绪化的后朋克切片，主题围绕与同一个人年复一年反复陷入又脱离爱情的循环。乐队列出的参考对象包括 Joy Division、She Past Away 和 Molchat Doma，表明其风格扎根于经典后朋克与暗潮传统。项目自 2025 年起持续以单曲形式发行作品，2026 年加快了发行节奏，《Sowe》是其第六张单曲及本年度第三张作品，整体维持稳定的暗黑后朋克输出路线。

items.body:
Smacking that sweetspot between grime, techno, bassline and soca, Anthoney J Hart (East Man, Imaginary Forces) aka Basic Rhythm delivers a full-bore pack of rampers for Bristol-via-Berlin’s bassbin overlords, Sneaker Social Club.

Active in a vein of uchronic, ‘nuum-bending invention since the 2010’s, but with roots reaching back to ‘90s pirate radio, Hart’s decade-straddling steez yields the crankiest horsepower as Basic Rhythm on ‘8 Bar Techno’. Hewing hard to the brief, he dissects and recombines styles & patterns with a fiercely upfront quality, trampling on putative borders with a rudeboy alacrity that works a treat on up-for -it ‘floors.

The durable torsion of OG jungle tekno and its myriad derivations are twisted into tensile girders, variously splitting the difference between 4/4 grime and hard groove techno in ‘the title tune, or panel-beating sublow into rictus bashiness on ‘Weed Killer’, while firing killer rounds of vocal cuts including the dancehall-grime of ‘Vibez’ with NyNy, or electroid drill with Lyrical Strally and Eklipse.

Along with the precision-tooled rufige of ‘Kонец века’ with Moscow Legend, the mutant soca gallop o ‘Ice cold’, and diesel-fuelled grime-techno of ‘More Pricks than Kicks’, or the dive-bombing darkness of ‘The Deluge’, it’s a hard set for discerning 140BPM shotters, and surely one of Basic Rhythm’s deadliest.

items.body:
Following her acclaimed 2022 album 'Weather Alive', Beth Orton returns with another fully self-produced collection of songs, this time bringing in help from Shahzad Ismaily, Vernon Spring's Sam Beste, drummers Chris Vatalaro and Vishal Nayak, trumpet player Christos Styliandes and bassist Tom Herbert.

Orton sounded refreshed on 'Weather Alive'. Taking the production into her own hands for the first time, she crafted a personal world that was completely her own, weaving in old recordings of her parents and recording a busted piano she snapped up at Camden Market. The music felt like a form of catharsis, dreamily reflecting on years of boozing and raving, when she made her mark as a guest vocalist for artists like the Chemical Brothers and William Orbit. That mature, knowing air - the kind of mettle you build up only after real-world experience - hangs around 'The Ground Above', giving Orton's tender, heartfelt songs genuine power and proper weight. When she sings "I'm as invincible as grief, dancing cross a lake of loss," on the epic opener 'The Ground Above', you don't doubt her for a moment.

Orton's voice has always been distinct, a soulful rasp that's fragile one moment and sturdy the next, and it sounds as if she's finally found the right music to match it. On that eight-minute opener, it's quick syncopated drums that lodge themselves somewhere between Roni Size's 'New Forms' and Radiohead's 'Hail to the Thief', reversed, psychedelic guitar riffs, jazzy horn blasts and pillowy ambient textures. 'Cigarette Curls', meanwhile, slows things down, pairing her voice with smudged piano phrases and smoke-y rhythms. She breezes past the shape of classic soul pop on 'Waiting', even taking on a half-sung chorus, but sounds most comfortable when she strips down the instrumentation even further, crooning over brushed percussion and euphoric pads on the gorgeous 'I'll Miss You'.
items._genre: indie folk / art pop / experimental pop
items._cn_summary: 这是Beth Orton继2022年备受好评的《Weather Alive》之后推出的第二张全自我制作的专辑，她邀请了Shahzad Ismaily等多位乐手协助录制。整张作品延续了上张专辑那种成熟的、内省的氛围，Orton以她独特的沙哑嗓音承载着经过岁月沉淀的情感表达。八分钟的开篇曲将切分鼓点、迷幻吉他、爵士铜管与蓬松的氛围音色交织在一起，借鉴了Roni Size到Radiohead等多种元素。后续曲目中，她时而以烟雾缭绕的钢琴与节奏搭配，时而剥离编曲仅留刷过的打击乐与氛围垫底，在简约与丰满之间游走。整张专辑展现出她在独立民谣与艺术流行之间开辟个人语汇的能力，情感真挚，编曲细腻，但整体仍偏向主流独立音乐范畴。

items.body:
Will Long dons his dancing slippers for another deep house sojourn on his Long Trax Productions, blowing kisses in the direction of Larry Heard, Ron Trent, DJ Sprinkles.

One decade since minting the ‘Long Trax’ series on Terre Thaemlitz’s label, Comatonse, Will Long slow cooks six new additions on his personal folio, taking all the time needed to get right into the groove. Trust there’s no fireworks or over-produced trickery, just hypnotic deep house that unfurls with a real sense of space, patience and deferred gratification.

Long in his element, following his nose to pair the barest ingredients in classic style and pattern, as with with the likes of ‘About Where It's At (Now You Went N' Did It mix)’, which takes over 4 mins happily swinging away before introducing its lonesome flute motif, or a standout ‘Have to Have Something’ lost in the flow, where the bassline only thickens as it goes along. 

We’re also partial to the square bass budge of ‘Have To Have Something (S' a Lotta Shade mix)’, and the mesmerising meld of creamy bass and piquant cowbell pinging on ‘The Problems’, also found warped with trippier effect on its Metallic Dub reshape.
items._cn_summary: Will Long 以 Long Trax Productions 名义发行第六张个人厂牌作品，延续其自 2014 年在 Terre Thaemlitz 旗下 Comatonse 创立的同名系列以来的创作脉络。整张专辑以六首曲目为主轴，强调空间感、耐心与延迟满足的制作理念，没有任何过度修饰或炫技成分。制作手法偏向极简，深沉的低音线条与少量配器元素缓慢铺陈：如一首曲子在前四分多钟仅以摆动律动推进，随后才引入孤独的长笛动机；另一首则让贝斯线在行进中逐步加厚。配器组合包括方块感低音、奶油质贝斯与清脆牛铃的交织，部分曲目另附有更具迷幻感的混音版本。整体致敬对象指向 Larry Heard、Ron Trent 与 DJ Sprinkles 等深层浩室经典人物，风格稳健但实验性有限。

items.body:
Lushest, hair-kissing deep house and Detroit techno by Kennedy, rolled out effortlessly smooth but kinky and flush with kaotic harmonies on his Dream Machine

Swinging in the breezy wake of chops for Music For Memory and and Pacific Rhythm, ‘Dream 5’ maintains a classic sound on his own label with two sides of the same Motor City-via-Amsterdam currency. A-side ‘Eclipse’ is a conga and pad-led swanger in the mold of Mike Grant’s Moods & Grooves, beautifully suspending hips and limbs in a lip-smcakcing deep house dream sequence, whereas B-side ‘Sky Things’ trades in a sort of deferred gratification, building it up like Derrick May via AGCG/808 State with kinky 727 drum patterns and sky-kissing kaotic harmonies to tease the ‘floor right where you want it.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP呈现两种密歇根底特律式的深沉舞曲取向，A面'Eclipse'以康加鼓与柔和pad音色铺陈，节奏松弛而诱人，让人联想到Moods & Grooves厂牌的经典深屋质感；B面'Sky Things'则转向更具张力的构建逻辑，分解式打击与升腾的和声层逐步推进，融合Derrick May式的techno骨架与更现代的合成器处理。整体在经典深屋与底特律techno之间取得平衡，编曲精巧但未涉及明显实验结构或先锋手法，声音设计偏向已有类型框架内的精致打磨。独立厂牌发行保证了地下属性，但风格定位偏向俱乐部舞曲传统，对追求前卫融合或即兴结构的听众吸引力有限。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将九十年代垃圾摇滚与另类摇滚的质感作为素材来源，与文艺复兴式的旋律线条并置，再以解构流行音乐结构的方式重新拼接。评论强调其拼贴技法的当代性，把多种本不相干的美学强行缝合，产生出一种既陌生又熟悉的效果。Escho是偏向实验与小众声音的厂牌，发行语境支持了这类非主流的创作方向。整体而言，专辑在融合层面有一定野心，但评论文本极短，缺乏对具体作品层次与声音细节的展开，使得这张作品在实验深度上仍难以充分确认。对于偏好前卫与跨界融合的听众而言，这张专辑值得留意，但从已有信息来看，还不足以判断其在声音设计或艺术视角上达到了多高的独创性。

100% killer reissue of Bim Sherman’s self-released 1988 dub masterpiece ‘Ghetto Dub’, mixed by King Tubby, Prince Jammy and Adrian Sherwood who diffuse rhythms by The Roots Radics and Sly & Robbie, newly remastered for its first new edition in 30 years.

With 2nd hand prices understandably climbing into triple figures, this overdue first vinyl reissue will be mana to the fiends. It takes pride of place in an ongoing programme of resurrected Sherman aces to portray him at his most elusive and atmospheric, or as the hype sticker calls it, “a journey in echo and space”.

His legendarily tone is threaded thru the desk by a team of JA/UK titans with the man himself in the producer role, sifting cuts from his Century Records: a label set up in the Uk in 1984, after his move from Kingston, JA, to London, where he became a crucial figure in the On-U Sound crew after joining their 1979 tour, and would lend to classic Dub Syndicate cuts among others. 

The record’s renown has grown over the years since Sherman’s passing in 2000 and the effective dissolution of his label. Week-End Records now do a sterling job of preserving his legacy with this edition, richly representing the warmth and pressure of the OG in its entirety, from the clean-spurred, buoyant step of its title tune to moon-booted ‘Untitled Dub’, via the soul-tugging ace ’Station Dub’ with its unanswered doorbells, and best showcase of his voice in ‘Moving Dub’, another alright stepper in ‘World Dub’, the bloozy wooze of ‘Danger Dub’ and wickedly skewed Afro-lilt of ‘Tribulation Dub.’

All killer.

items.body:
In their sublime duo debut the simpatico synth & guitar of Jonny Nash & Tomo Katsurada is seduces to blissed, wind-whispering soundscapes, hashed out over the course of 12 months since Katsurada lent strings to Nash’s ‘Once Was Our Forever’. Dream material FFO Ghost, Makoto Kawabata, Joanne Robertson...

"Netherlands-based artists Tomo Katsurada (Ex-Kikagaku Moyo / Future Days Radio) and Jonny Nash (Melody As Truth) combine forces for an exploration into the sonic potential of the guitar duo, rooted in their experiences performing together over the last 12 months.

Friends and admirers of each other’s work for a decade, their musical collaboration began in 2024 with Katsurada asking Nash to contribute guitar to his debut EP ‘Dream Of The Egg’. Sensing the need to explore this further, they spent the following year performing together in different configurations, with Nash joining Katsurada’s trio and Katsurada in turn playing with Nash as a duo, across a wide spectrum of spaces, from churches and temples to concert halls, theatres and outdoor festivals. With new ideas developing organically out of these performances, recording new material became the next logical step. A short period of three days was set aside with a clear goal: to capture the essence of their fluid, intertwining melodies and guitar playing in a way that felt as direct and unfiltered as possible. Working from a handful of pre-existing sketches, they left ample room for experimentation to unfold within the process.

The results are presented on ‘At The Emerald Pool’, a collection of ten pieces that offer the listener a full immersion into the pair’s sound. With guitar as the primary instrument for both artists, it is no surprise that the core of the album lies here, specifically in the fluid interplay between the two players. Layers of gentle, delay-soaked fingerpicking often make it almost impossible to distinguish where one player ends and the other begins. As soloists, both Katsurada and Nash have a gift for crafting melodic lines that feel open and ascending, expressive and hopeful without becoming saccharine. Longer, more abstract pieces are counterbalanced by a series of shorter songs, with five vocal tracks appearing across the album. The decision to share vocal duties lends the record a unique quality and a strong sense of variation, bringing a wide expressive range out of a deliberately focused musical framework.

‘At The Emerald Pool’ represents the first chapter in an ongoing musical dialogue, an attempt to capture a moment of connection, openness and discovery, laying the foundation for what continues to unfold."

A constant point of reference, Sacred Harp S
items.body:
An early prime cat # number, DEATH013 marks the label’s 1st survey of Sacred Harp Singing, a tradition of sacred choral music stemming from New England and developed in the US Deep South, where its a cappella style has taken root as native music

DINTE did, and continue, to do the Lord’s work with ‘I’m on My Journey Home: Sacred Harp Singing, 1928-1934’ and its many follow-up volumes parsed, with love and attentive ear, from C.20th annals and archives. A constant point of reference, Sacred Harp Singing is among the purest, unaccompanied forms of songcraft from the Deep South; one which has transcended its church origins to become beloved as a cultural artefact of the region spanning Georgia to Alabama and - as often indicated by the groups’ names. To sink into the sound is to be transported to past lives, and the past as a foreign land, and be transfixed by its songs of devotion and hope.
items._genre: sacred harp singing / a cappella / american folk
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由Deathbomb Arc旗下子厂牌发行的Sacred Harp圣咏合辑，收录1928至1934年间美国南部地区的原始录音。Sacred Harp是一种源自新英格兰、在美国深南部扎根的无伴奏合唱传统，其纯粹的无乐器声乐形式被视为该地区最重要的文化声音遗产之一。合辑从二十世纪档案文献中精心挑选片段，试图还原一种跨越教堂起源、成为佐治亚至阿拉巴马地区文化象征的音乐实践。这些录音承载着信徒虔诚的情感与早期录音技术的粗粝质感，使听众能够感受到一种跨越时空的虔诚氛围。整体而言，这是一份具有重要文献价值的早期音乐档案，面向对民间传统和地方文化研究有兴趣的听众，而非追求实验或前卫声响的听众。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
In 2026, I was invited to join the Silkroad Ensemble, the international collective directed by Rhiannon Giddens, as a musician (frame drums, violin, and voice) and contributor of new arrangements and compositions. Following an initial workshop and preview performance in New York in January 2026, the project will unfold through a North American tour in March 2026, featuring nine concerts alongside workshops and community outreach activities across the United States, as part of the new program
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
. The tour will continue later in the year with further residencies and performances in North America and Europe.
There are musical projects that are built around a repertoire, others around a geography, and others still around a specific aesthetic vision. The Silkroad Ensemble belongs to a different category: it is a living organism built around an idea. A simple and radical idea at once�that music can be a real space of encounter between cultures, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a daily, concrete, lived practice.
Founded in 1998 by Yo-Yo Ma, Silkroad has never been an ensemble in the traditional sense. There is no fixed lineup, no stable repertoire. Instead, it is a community of musicians from different traditions, chosen not only for their technical excellence, but for their ability to inhabit a threshold�the space between rootedness and transformation. Each musician brings with them a language, a sound, a memory. What matters most is the willingness to place that language in dialogue with others, without hierarchy.
In recent years, the project has been guided by Rhiannon Giddens, one of the most powerful and deeply insightful voices in contemporary music. Her presence gives the work a clear direction: the goal is not to create an artificial synthesis of traditions, but to create the conditions for each tradition to speak fully, and to transform through encounter. Rhiannon possesses a rare kind of leadership�one that never imposes itself, but quietly shapes the space, both musically and humanly.
Entering this context means immediately finding yourself in a space where musical identity is not something to defend, but something to offer. The pizzica, the frame drums, the violin I carry with me are no longer only instruments of a local tradition, but elements in a broader conversation, where every sound is heard both for what it is and for what it might become.
It is within this space that my participation in Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual began to take shape. Even before the music itself, what stands out is the quality of listening. A real, deep listening, in which every musical gesture is at once personal and collective. This, perhaps, is the true nature of Silkroad: not simply an ensemble, but a place. A circle. A space where music returns to what it has always been�a form of relationship.
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
Music as Refuge and Resistance
The word sanctuary can be understood in many ways: refuge, protected space, a place where it is still possible to pause, to listen, to rebuild a sense of community.
Working on this project in the United States today carries a particular weight. This is a country marked by deep and increasingly visible tensions, where public discourse is often shaped by fear, by closure, by the idea that identity is something to be defended against someone else. The same tendency can be seen elsewhere�in Italy, across Europe, and in many parts of the world. The rise of nationalism, ongoing wars, and increasingly restrictive migration policies contribute to a climate in which separation begins to feel like the natural order of things.
Within this context, finding yourself in a room each day with musicians from Morocco, India, Japan, Armenia, Scotland, Congo, Italy, and the United States becomes something very real. Each person brings their own history, their own sound, their own way of inhabiting music. What emerges is not a fusion of identities, but their coexistence.
The taranta, Gnawa music, Indian classical tradition, American folk music�these practices were never conceived merely as forms of entertainment. They were born as tools to accompany moments of transformation, to help individuals and communities move through crisis, grief, healing, and renewal.
Sanctuary begins with this understanding. With the idea that music can still be a space where encounter is possible without the need to simplify or protect oneself. A space where listening becomes an act of trust.
Something simple and real happens: people from different parts of the world breathe together, listen together, and build something that did not exist before. In a time that often pushes toward division, this act acquires a different weight. It becomes, in its own quiet way, a form of resistance.
Entering the Circle
The first rehearsals are always a delicate moment. I took part in an initial workshop in Ireland last December, with a smaller group�Rhiannon, Mazz, Francesco, Niwel, and myself�and then a second workshop with the full ensemble in January, followed by a beautiful preview performance in New York on January 10, 2026, as part of the Winter Jazz Fest.
At that stage, there is no shared language yet. You observe each other, you play, you try things, you listen. What strikes you immediately is the extraordinary musical and human level of the people involved. They are incredible. Not only great instrumentalists, but musicians who have developed a deep relationship with their own musical traditions, and who have learned to question them, to keep them flexible and alive.
The Hawaiian bassist Shawn Conley, for example, moves effortlessly between bow and pizzicato, shifting from a lyrical, singing tone to remarkable rhythmic agility, using the instrument with a freedom that easily recalls the expressive range of a cello.
Beside him, Scottish harpist Maeve Gilchrist brings a presence that is both refined and fearless. Beyond a complete mastery of everything one might expect from the harp�the luminous, almost celestial sound�she possesses an extraordinary rhythmic and harmonic awareness, and a musical curiosity that allows her to make bold, unexpected choices without hesitation.
Armenian cellist Karen Ouzounian represents the very highest level of classical tradition, but with something more: a strong personal voice, a deep compositional sensibility, and a lyrical approach to improvisation that makes every gesture feel necessary.
With Francesco Turrisi, who like me comes from Italy, we already share a longer history. Yet I remain constantly struck by his ability to move between radically different instruments�accordion, piano, frame drums, string instruments�with complete naturalness. His immense musicality is not tied to any single instrument, but to a broader understanding of sound, form, and structure.
Congolese guitarist Niwel Tsumbu is simply one of the finest guitarists I have ever encountered. His relationship with the guitar transcends the instrument itself. He brings together a deep knowledge of African musical traditions, an innate rhythmic sensibility, refined harmonic awareness, and an extraordinary improvisational freedom.
Kaoru Watanabe embodies, in a profound way, the idea that tradition is also a choice. Japanese and American, he moves fluidly between cultural languages with a rare balance of respect, discipline, and expressive freedom. His playing is never a reproduction of the past, but its living continuation.
With Mehdi Nassouli, on guembri and voice, I feel a particular closeness. Like me with pizzica, he belongs deeply to a specific musical world�in his case, the Gnawa tradition of Morocco. Yet his experience has given him an equally deep ability to engage in dialogue with other musical languages, without ever losing the center of his own sound.
Sandeep Das�s presence on tabla is a constant point of reference. He is, quite literally, a guru of Indian music, and yet his authority never creates distance. On the contrary, he makes every interaction feel natural, effortless, both musically and humanly.
Japanese percussionist Haruka Fujii brings an extraordinary level of precision and listening. Her virtuosity is never displayed for its own sake, but always placed in service of the music, strengthening the cohesion of the ensemble.
American violinist and vocalist Mazz Swift embodies a rare combination of strength and openness. Their voice and violin move fluidly across genres and traditions, grounded yet constantly searching, expanding the expressive space of the group.
And then there is Rhiannon. It is difficult to find a single word that captures her presence. She is a complete musician�singer, instrumentalist, composer, dancer, and leader�but above all, she possesses a clarity of vision that holds everything together and inspires everyone around her. Her leadership does not operate through control, but through listening. She creates a space in which each musician can fully express themselves, while contributing to something larger than any individual voice.
Common Ground
"Common Ground" is the pizzica I wrote for the Silkroad Ensemble. I use the word �wrote� with caution, because the piece truly exists only through the creative contribution of each musician involved. I laid the foundations: the rhythm, the groove, the structure, the overall architecture, and the fixed melodic and harmonic elements. But what makes it alive is the way each musician inhabits it.
The idea first emerged during the workshop in Ireland. At that stage, we were still searching for common ground, a way of being together musically without renouncing our individual identities. It felt natural for me to bring the rhythm of pizzica�my familiar and chosen refuge, my Sanctuary.
Back home, I began to develop that intuition, shaping a structure that preserved the physical and rhythmic core of the tradition, while remaining open enough to allow each musician to find their own place within it. We worked on the piece during the workshop in the United States, and performed it live for the first time in New York, just days later, at the Winter Jazz Fest.
It was extraordinary to witness how naturally each musician entered that rhythm without hesitation. No one was trying to imitate something that did not belong to them. Instead, each voice emerged clearly, freely coexisting alongside the others.
In that moment, I understood that the piece had found its true meaning. It was no longer simply the pizzica I had written, but a shared space. A Common Ground laid beneath our feet.
Experiences like this change you in subtle but lasting ways. The energy they transmit, the enthusiasm, the renewed sense of trust in the future�all of it remains.
A few years ago, I was in Adelaide to perform at WOMAD with Justin Adams, and the night before our concert I had the chance to attend a performance by Billy Bragg. At one point, he said something that has stayed with me ever since: �Music does not have the power to change the world. But it can make you believe that the world can be changed.�

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 2026 sees the release of Muse's most relevant and diverse studio album in about two decades or so.'The Wow! Signal' is the tenth full-length studio recording from the British alternative rockdarlings and sees them bringing in producer Dan Lancaster for the first time around. Pushing thetrio to pursuit a more modern production, Lancaster definitely influenced the sound of this record,which exhibits certain similarities to other alternative bands like Bring Me the Horizon and ThreeDays Grace, with which Lancaster has also worked throughout the years. Thematically, 'The Wow!Signal' deals with space and cosmic mysteries, while some songs definitely feel like more personalstatements from Mat Bellamy. Calling this album "space rock" would then be inaccurate because itexhibits elements of alternative rock, art pop and electronic music, offering some truly proggyriffs and several unorthodox arrangements. 'The Wow! Signal' is a more of a typical maximalist Museventure that impresses with an overt-the-top energy and stunning production all throughout.In the light of this consideration, it is very interesting to hear all the different styles the bandcovers on this album. Opening their set with the unbridled and anthemic piece 'The Dark Forest', animmediate wave of nostalgic Muse pretentiousness overwhelms the listener with orchestralarrangements, anxious falsettos, and muscular guitar riffs. This is followed by 'NightshiftSuperstar', one of the most convincing singles released by the band in recent years, and anexcellent song that echoes the dance-pop aesthetic of Muse's last two albums. 'Cryogen' is anotherinteresting song that combines the art rock dynamics of earlier Muse with a futuristic electronicsound that once again reminisces the output of other contemporary alt-rock/metal acts. Later on weget 'Hexagons', which sounds like a sophisticated prog-pop number, and while it could have feltcompletely out of place on this album, the final result is actually impressive. Perhaps the mostenjoyable parts of 'The Wow! Signal' are the ones where Muse explore a darker alt-metal sound andthe tracks 'The Sickness in You & I' and 'Unravelling' are definitely fine examples. The EllieGoulding feature on 'Hush' is quite intriguing as well, as this duet actually turns out to be a veryenjoyable and unexpected entry!All in all, 'The Wow! Signal' achieves an excellent balance between modern production and nostalgicMuse maximalism. The arrangements, vocals, and overall instrumentation on this album are top-notch,and the entire thing feels like a coherent sonically intense work. On top of that, the trio deliverssome of their most compelling songs as of late. Excellent return to form from Muse!

Signal》由新制作人Dan Lancaster操刀，主题围绕太空与宇宙之谜展开，同时融入主唱Matt Bellamy的个人表达。专辑试图在现代制作与乐队一贯的古典管弦乐编排之间寻找平衡，运用交响编制、假声演唱和力量感吉他riff，开篇曲《The Dark Forest》和中段《Hexagons》展示了雄浑的能量，《Nightshift Superstar》则转向舞曲流行美学，Ellie Goulding参与的《Hush》构成一次对话式尝试。整体风格融合另类摇滚、艺术流行与电子元素，配器层次繁复，制作精良，但在声音探索上偏向安全的主流区域。

items.body: Devoratus, a darkwave band from Denver, Colorado, released the “Vacio” EP on 4 July 2026. The three-track record is sung in Spanish and English and is available to stream on Spotify. The title translates from Spanish as “empty” or “void.” The EP’s three tracks are “Abismo oscuro,” “Dance” and “For You.” The songs move between Spanish titles and lyrics and English refrains, the bilingual approach the band has used since its first releases in 2023. Across the three tracks the band addresses isolation, desire, mortality and change. Inside the Devoratus ‘Vacio’ EP Devoratus records as a trio of Tomas on vocals, Aero on synths and Renee on bass, with Cisco adding live guitar. On “Vacio” the arrangements pair cold synth lines and heavy low end with guitar and forward-driving drums. The band released the EP without a label credit, as a digital release; no physical edition has been announced. Musically the band can be compared to darkwave acts including Lebanon Hanover and She Past Away. About Devoratus Devoratus is a darkwave and post-punk band from Denver, Colorado. The band describes itself as a “Post Punk Darkwave Latino Band” and sings in both Spanish and English. Its recording lineup is Tomas on vocals, Aero on synths and Renee on bass, with Cisco on live guitar. The band began releasing music in 2023, starting with the single and video “Distancia” and the “Amissus” EP the same year. In February 2024 Devoratus issued the single “Flotando,” followed later in 2024 by the three-track “Vida Irreal” EP, made up of “Cold Night,” “Mal” and “Vampira.” Those earlier releases remain on the band’s Bandcamp page. With the “Vacio” EP on 4 July 2026, Devoratus continues the Spanish-and-English darkwave it has released since 2023.

items.body: Akusmi Terra Incognita Pascal Bideau’s latest album as Akusmi plays out like a collective expression of notional anthems from unknown lands, says Bernie Brooks Terra Incognita by Akusmi Just shy of a decade ago, I toured part of an automobile plant where trucks are assembled. While this was obviously a sanitised space intended for visitors, it was equally obvious that the place was far from a dark, satanic mill of yore. It was relatively bright and clean, and the work, while clearly skilled and not without risk, was well-paid. The factory – humans included – was less a collection of automated and operated industrial equipment and more like a single, giant mechanism. Or cyberorganism, maybe, each worker a part of the machine, filling roles... The post Akusmi – Terra Incognita appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Pascal Bideau以Akusmi名义发行的专辑《Terra Incognita》，乐评人Bernie Brooks将其描述为来自未知土地的假想颂歌的集合表达。文中以参观汽车装配工厂的经历作为切入点，将工厂——包括其中的人类——比作一个巨大的机械装置或赛博有机体，每个工人都是机器的一部分，各司其职。这段隐喻暗示了专辑在声音层面可能探讨机械化、人与系统之间的关系等主题。乐评整体偏短，主要内容为引言性质的场景铺设，尚未深入展开对专辑音乐本体——如音色设计、作曲手法、节奏编排等方面的具体分析。The Quietus作为以实验与先锋音乐为主的英国独立媒体，其选稿标准偏向非主流领域，Akusmi的厂牌背景和具体音乐细节在所提供的文本中未获充分披露，使得读者难以形成完整判断。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Someone is having a laugh, someone in Germany. My good friend Artur Chachlowski recently sent me this CD from Poland, and as you can see the name of the band is Welsh! Strange, I thought. All the lyrics are in English so that was a good start, but what was most unusual was the music! Here is a German band with a Welsh name sounding 100% English! And not very modern English at that! Llyn Y Morynion (hereafter called Llyn) are a progressive band mixing loads of influences, most of them English. Listen to the delicate ballad of "Poor Man's Child", with some wonderful classical guitar and haunting keyboards, and be stunned by the sheer beauty and majesty of the music. Conversely, be taken aback by the riffing power of "Drowned Day". Having played this a great deal, the band that I think that are most similar in the current scene is probably Legend, and even that link is tenuous. This album belongs more in the Seventies than the Nineties, but it also has a timeless quality, a feeling of being a classic. Unless they have an enormous stroke of luck, Llyn are going to release one of the best albums of the year (with some great packaging as well) and sell bugger all. If you like Legend, or Tull, or acoustic mixed with rock, oh hell, if you just like GREAT MUSIC then you owe it to yourself to get this.Originally appeared in Feedback#38, November 1996

items._cn_summary: 这张1993年的跨界前卫摇滚专辑来自一支以威尔士语命名的德国乐队，却呈现出浓郁的英式七十年代气息。乐评指出其音乐混合多种英式影响，既有民谣抒情曲风中精致的古典吉他与萦绕键盘，也有强力失真驱动的硬摇滚段落。评论者将其与Legend和Jethro Tull相提并论，认为作品具有经典气质和时代超越感，但同时也预见到商业上的冷遇。整体听感更接近七十年代传统前卫摇滚的怀旧路线，而非九十年代的现代前卫取向。

items.body: Review by Steve Conrad — Alt-rock/metal; Perceptive POVBut Is It Progressive?I stand on the mighty shoulders of Prog Archives expertise, who call SLUG COMPARISON music "crossover prog". To my ears, it sounds like alternative rock with metal touches, all with a keenly observant point of view, to be found on this newest release from FEN'S Doug Harrison.Nonetheless, this is another creative outpouring of music and poetic insights and imagery from Mr. Harrison, focusing, it seems to me, on the creative process- its costs and rewards and dangers.Some years ago I reviewed Slug Comparison's "When You Were Living Here" (2019), which resonated so deeply I thought it deserved five stars- it voiced the kind of grief and genuine, raw emotion of the worst kind of loss, in such tender and vulnerable ways.A Battle to the End...This album mines deep and insightful terrain, in quite different ways- and it too resonates. I'm impressed with Harrison's compositional mastery, the way he starts tracks in a variety of ways that draw us in, to the intensity jumping up notches with gritty guitar riffs, to soundscapes of synths or psychedelic-tinged lead guitars, to pulsing bass lines, to his excellent vocal work both in simple and quiet lines as well as ultra-high vocalizations.And these also meet considerable variety within the various tracks of this album. The title itself, "A Battle to the End Fought on the Edge of a Knife", suggests the kind of exquisitely difficult balancing act required when one factors in the demands of making a living, finding time to compose, to record, to fine-tune, to TRY to be a family person and a friend to others, to rehearse, and all while in this case, deal with what sounds like scoring high on the introversion scale!I can relate.Some Track Notes"Wish to Adapt" starts off the album with hushed but magnetic guitar and a whimsical guitar lead line (the album is chock-full of subtle and overt lines and counterpoints), then the restrained vocals with the lyrics lamenting how easy it seems to stay within the familiar lines and forms, and how tough it is to break free of these restraints. When the heavier chorus comes chiming in, the vocals get more intense, and Harrison shows considerable range and quality on the vocals- and the use of vocalizations as well. I hear the frustration, and a sense of impatience with self, and the desire to push the boundaries, to exceed what had come before."March Through the Forest" has a hypnotic, pulsating bass and synth line that draws us in, and I admire the imagery in such lines like, "tromping through the meadow popping swollen icy patches/ frozen little diamonds bedded in the ground"- the evocative lyrics are sheer poetry, as the protagonist- perhaps taking a breather from the "edge of the knife" hikes with a companion in the woods and mountains.For me, "Game of Repression" is among the stand-out tracks- It comes rip-roaring in with that gutsy guitar riff, then deftly shifts into the voice singing the struggle of managing the gritty and sometimes brutal emotions that can come forth unbidden and oft-times unwanted. Again, I'm impressed with the kind of deft revelation of the creative inner world, "I wanna be innocuous, I wanna be kind/ I wanna be an enemy to absolutely no one/ but now and then I tend to malign/ reminding me I'm losing at the game of repression".Well, sheesh. Who hasn't blurted out something utterly reprehensible and deeply regretted?Wait, There's More!This review could turn into a term-paper, so let's move ahead- you get the idea! The other standout track I'll consider (and there are numerous other standouts) is "Metal Roots Came Twisting". This one partly inspired my characterization of this music as "alternative rock with metal touches". Well damn! I love every part of this track, starting with the seductive soft opening guitar, then the semi-counterpoint lead line, the way it builds from fairly straight forward vocals into more gutsy textures, and with such whimsy and subtle humor in lines like, "love, peace, yet I felt so ill at ease/ flubbing the off beats every time/ hey, mon, singers faking Jamaican/ I couldn't feel the groove/ I couldn't hear their blissed-out muse/ and metal roots came twisting through my arms"- all while throwing down a supposed reggae vibe, and a few suggestions in the voice of "singers faking Jamaican" (Call The Police??).So Let's Sum UpI think this one is a fine addition to any music collection- I'll leave it to you listeners to agree or disagree with Prog Archives or my own suggested genres. I find the entire album an excellent aural and lyrical experience of living a creative life in a human form!
items._genre: crossover prog / alternative rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由FEN乐队的Doug Harrison主导创作，以另类摇滚为底色融入金属质感与合成器音景，主题围绕创作过程的艰辛与内心挣扎展开。乐评指出Harrison在作曲上展现出多样化的手法：从低调磁性的吉他引入，到粗粝的吉他riff爆发，再到迷幻色彩的主音吉他与脉动贝斯线，层次丰富。人声演绎兼顾安静低吟与高亢嘶喊，歌词富有诗意与画面感，如林间漫步的意象描写。评论者对Harrison的声音设计与作曲掌控力给予肯定，尤其赞赏'Game of Repression'等曲目的张力。然而整体风格偏向渐进摇滚框架内的抒情表达，虽有织体变化，但在声音实验性与结构突破方面较为有限，与极端前卫或实验音乐的距离较远。
